ig_carousel_topic.topic: Why your win rate matters less than your ROI
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
54% win rate. Losing money.
62% win rate. Also losing money.
How is that possible?
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors fixate on win rate.
Win more than you lose and you're profitable. Simple, right?
Not quite. The odds attached to each bet change everything.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
ROI accounts for what you actually collect per dollar risked.
A 54% win rate at +110 average odds beats a 60% win rate at -145.
The payout structure is the variable most bettors ignore.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: 100 bets at -145, 62 wins, 38 losses.
Return: 62 x 100 minus 38 x 145 = 6,200 minus 5,510 = +690.
Same 100 bets at +110, 54 wins: 54 x 110 minus 46 x 100 = 5,940 minus 4,600 = +1,340.
Lower win rate. Nearly double the profit.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
Our YTD: 243-204, 54.4% win rate, +37.7u, 9.3% ROI across 41 days.
Win rate tells you one number. ROI tells you the whole story.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win rate is the stat everyone watches. ROI is the one that actually matters. The math is simpler than it looks.
